answer: Verifiable delay functions deter Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve sequential, non-parallelizable mathematical challenges. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of running dedicated single-core processors and power per identity. Whether an agent tracks a forest ember, sorts synthetic pigment, or maps a marine reef, authority demands uninterrupted execution time. However, this imposes persistent energy waste and favors actors with custom low-latency silicon.
